Meaning: Vigilant awareness of Allah that produces reverence, obedience, and restraint from sin. It includes the sense of protecting oneself from divine displeasure, so neither "fear" nor "piety" alone is sufficient.
Arabic variations + translation: اِتَّقَى (verb) — avoid; guard against | مُتَّقٍ (active participle) — God-conscious; pious | المُتَّقُون (plural) — the God-conscious; the pious

Meaning: Spiritual and moral excellence, especially worshipping Allah with deep awareness and treating creation well. It is broader than ordinary kindness.
Arabic variations + translation: أَحْسَنَ (verb) — do good; do excellently | مُحْسِن (active participle) — doer of good; benefactor | مُحْسِنُون (plural) — doers of good; benefactors

Meaning: Assigning to another what belongs exclusively to Allah, especially worship or divine authority. It includes obvious and subtle forms, not only belief in several gods.
Arabic variations + translation: أَشْرَكَ (verb) — associate partners; ascribe a partner | مُشْرِك (active participle) — polytheist; one who associates partners | مُشْرِكُون (plural) — polytheists; those who associate partners

Meaning: Purifying worship and intention from all rivals and self-display. It is exclusive devotion to Allah, not frankness alone.
Arabic variations + translation: أَخْلَصَ (verb) — make sincere; devote exclusively | مُخْلِص (active participle) — sincere; devoted

Meaning: The divinely ordained way of faith, worship, ethics, and accountability. Depending on context, the same word can also mean judgment or recompense.
Arabic variations + translation: دَانَ بِـ (verb) — profess; adhere to | دِينِيّ (adjective) — religious; pertaining to religion
Alternative context meaning(s): Different vocalization (الدَّيْن): debt; an obligation owed.

Meaning: The original God-given human disposition that is receptive to truth and worship. It is not every natural impulse or acquired social habit.
Arabic variations + translation: فِطْرِيّ (nisba adjective) — innate; natural | فِطْرِيَّة (abstract noun) — innateness; naturalness

Meaning: The human condition of devoted servitude and complete dependence on Allah. Although the literal root relates to servitude, the theological sense is honourable worshipful belonging, not human enslavement.
Arabic variations + translation: عَبَدَ (verb) — worship; serve | عَابِد (active participle) — worshipper; devotee

Meaning: Reverent humility and attentive stillness of the heart and body before Allah, especially in prayer. It combines inward presence, submission, and outward composure.
Arabic variations + translation: خَشَعَ (verb) — humble oneself; submit reverently | خَاشِع (active participle) — humble; devout

Meaning: Reliance of the heart on Allah while using lawful and effective means. It rejects both passive fatalism and treating worldly causes as independently sufficient.
Arabic variations + translation: تَوَكَّلَ عَلَى (verb) — rely on; entrust oneself to | مُتَوَكِّل (active participle) — reliant; trusting

Meaning: Remembering or mentioning Allah, receiving a reminder, or the revealed reminder itself. Context can refer to devotional remembrance, the Qur'an, or moral recollection.
Arabic variations + translation: ذَكَرَ (verb) — remember; mention | ذَاكِر (active participle) — one who remembers; remembering

Meaning: Calling upon Allah through request, praise, or worship. It usually means supplication and is distinct from the formal ritual prayer.
Arabic variations + translation: دَعَا (verb) — call upon; supplicate | دَاعٍ (active participle) — caller; supplicant

Meaning: Losing or departing from the path of right guidance. It can range from confusion to culpable rejection and is stronger than an ordinary mistake.
Arabic variations + translation: ضَلَّ (verb) — go astray; err | ضَالّ (active participle) — astray; misguided | ضَالُّون (plural) — the misguided; those astray

Meaning: A context-dependent term for a test, temptation, persecution, destabilizing trial, punishment, or civil strife. Its central image is a process that exposes or tests what is genuine.
Arabic variations + translation: فَتَنَ (verb) — test; tempt | مَفْتُون (passive participle) — captivated; infatuated

Meaning: A test permitted or decreed by Allah that reveals a person's response and may refine character. It can occur through hardship or prosperity, not only calamity.
Arabic variations + translation: اِبْتَلَى (verb) — test; try | مُبْتَلًى (passive participle) — tested; afflicted

Meaning: The unseen realm inaccessible to ordinary direct perception. It includes realities known through revelation, not simply what humans have not discovered yet.
Arabic variations + translation: غَابَ (verb) — be absent; disappear | غَائِب (active participle) — absent; missing

Meaning: Allah's measured decree and apportionment of creation and events. Unlike blind fate, it is connected with divine knowledge, will, measure, and creation.
Arabic variations + translation: قَدَّرَ (verb) — measure; decree | مُقَدَّر (passive participle) — measured; decreed

Meaning: A decisive judgment, completion, or enactment. In theology it can refer to Allah's decree taking effect; in law it can mean judicial judgment, so context is essential.
Arabic variations + translation: قَضَى (verb) — decide; judge | قَاضٍ (noun) — judge; adjudicator

Meaning: Divine will by which events occur or do not occur. It is an effective will, not an uncertain wish.
Arabic variations + translation: شَاءَ (verb) — will; wish

Meaning: Reverent fear arising from knowledge of Allah's greatness and one's responsibility before Him. It carries a stronger sense of awe and recognition than ordinary fear.
Arabic variations + translation: خَشِيَ (verb) — fear; revere | خَاشٍ (active participle) — fearful; reverent

Meaning: Steadfast uprightness upon faith without deviating to extremes. It is comprehensive consistency in creed, worship, and conduct.
Arabic variations + translation: اِسْتَقَامَ (verb) — be upright; remain straight | مُسْتَقِيم (adjective) — upright; steadfast

Meaning: Serenity and stabilizing assurance bestowed by Allah, especially during fear or upheaval. It is an inward settling of the heart rather than ordinary quiet.
Arabic variations + translation: سَكَنَ (verb) — become still; settle | سَاكِن (adjective) — still; calm

Meaning: Whatever provision Allah apportions, including material resources, health, knowledge, opportunity, and spiritual benefit. It is broader than salary or income.
Arabic variations + translation: رَزَقَ (verb) — provide; sustain | رَازِق (active participle) — provider; sustainer

Meaning: A resemblance or uncertainty that makes falsehood appear plausible or a ruling appear doubtful. It can refer to intellectual confusion or an ambiguous matter.
Arabic variations + translation: اِشْتَبَهَ (verb) — be unclear; resemble | مُشْتَبِه (adjective) — ambiguous; doubtful

Meaning: Scrupulous restraint from doubtful or spiritually harmful matters. It is cautious moral self-protection beyond bare legality.
Arabic variations + translation: تَوَرَّعَ (verb) — abstain scrupulously; be cautious | مُتَوَرِّع (active participle) — scrupulous; abstinent

Meaning: The Prophet's normative teaching, practice, and approved way; in other contexts, an established practice or recurring divine pattern. The intended sense must be determined from context.
Arabic variations + translation: سَنَّ (verb) — institute a practice; establish a precedent

Meaning: A practice introduced into religion as worship without a valid basis. In this sermon context, it does not refer to every new tool, technology, or ordinary custom.
Arabic variations + translation: اِبْتَدَعَ (verb) — innovate; originate | مُبْتَدِع (active participle) — innovator; originator

Meaning: A qualified scholar's nonbinding legal answer to a religious question. It differs from a court judgment, which can be legally enforceable.
Arabic variations + translation: أَفْتَى (verb) — issue a legal opinion; give a fatwa | مُفْتٍ (noun) — mufti; legal scholar

Meaning: The divinely revealed path encompassing faith, worship, ethics, and law. Reducing it to criminal penalties or court rules seriously narrows the concept.
Arabic variations + translation: شَرَعَ (verb) — prescribe; legislate | شَرْعِيّ (adjective) — legal; Sharia-related

Meaning: Disciplined reasoning by a qualified scholar to derive or apply a religious ruling. It is not unrestricted personal opinion.
Arabic variations + translation: اِجْتَهَدَ (verb) — exert independent reasoning; strive intellectually | مُجْتَهِد (noun) — independent jurist; mujtahid

Meaning: Following a qualified juristic authority without independently deriving the proof. It is technical reliance, not necessarily mindless copying.
Arabic variations + translation: قَلَّدَ (verb) — imitate; follow | مُقَلِّد (active participle) — follower; imitator

Meaning: A decisive proof that establishes truth and responsibility. It denotes evidence that leaves no valid excuse, not rhetorical debate.
Arabic variations + translation: اِحْتَجَّ (verb) — argue; cite as proof
Alternative context meaning(s): Different vocalization (الحِجَّة): one pilgrimage; a performance of Hajj.

Meaning: Divine communication conveyed to a prophet in the manner Allah chooses. It is authoritative revelation, not private intuition or creative inspiration.
Arabic variations + translation: أَوْحَى (verb) — reveal; communicate discreetly | مُوحًى (passive participle) — revealed; communicated
Alternative context meaning(s): General Arabic: a discreet signal; a quick communication or suggestion.

Meaning: A contextually justified interpretation, final outcome, or ultimate realization of a text or event. Classical usage is broader than free allegorical interpretation.
Arabic variations + translation: أَوَّلَ (verb) — interpret; explain an intended outcome | مُؤَوِّل (active participle) — interpreter; one who interprets

Meaning: A heart-directed admonition combining teaching, warning, encouragement, and compassionate counsel. Its aim is moral awakening, not information alone.
Arabic variations + translation: وَعَظَ (verb) — admonish; exhort | وَاعِظ (noun) — preacher; admonisher

Meaning: Inviting people to Allah with knowledge, wisdom, and suitable means. It is principled invitation, not coercion or publicity alone.
Arabic variations + translation: دَعَا (verb) — invite; call | دَاعِيَة (noun) — preacher; caller
Alternative context meaning(s): Social context: invitation, such as to a meal or event.

Meaning: What revelation and sound custom recognize as right, fitting, and socially honourable. It is more than whatever is familiar.
Arabic variations + translation: عَرَفَ (verb) — know; recognize

Meaning: What revelation and sound moral judgment recognize as wrong or unacceptable. It is not simply something unfamiliar.
Arabic variations + translation: أَنْكَرَ (verb) — deny; disapprove

Meaning: Giving each person or matter its due and judging without bias or excess. Justice does not always require identical treatment when relevant circumstances differ.
Arabic variations + translation: عَدَلَ (verb) — act justly; deal fairly | عَادِل (adjective) — just; fair

Meaning: Manifest fairness that gives each party its due. It stresses enacted and measurable justice, especially in dealings and testimony.
Arabic variations + translation: أَقْسَطَ (verb) — act justly; deal equitably | مُقْسِط (adjective) — just; equitable

Meaning: Rejecting, denying, or covering over divine truth. The word has theological and legal uses, and applying it to particular people requires context and care.
Arabic variations + translation: كَفَرَ (verb) — disbelieve; reject | كَافِر (noun) — disbeliever; unbeliever | كَافِرُون (plural) — disbelievers; unbelievers
Alternative context meaning(s): Moral/lexical context: ingratitude; denial of a favour, without necessarily meaning theological disbelief.

Meaning: A prohibited increase or exchange imbalance defined by Islamic commercial law. It includes many forms of interest but is a wider juristic category than the English word alone.
Arabic variations + translation: رَبَا (verb) — increase; grow | رِبَوِيّ (adjective) — usurious; interest-based

Meaning: The obligatory, calculated share of qualifying wealth given to designated recipients. It is a legal right of recipients, not merely voluntary charity.
Arabic variations + translation: زَكَا (verb) — grow; become pure | زَكَّى (verb) — purify; give zakat on

Meaning: A trust or responsibility that must be faithfully protected and fulfilled. It includes entrusted property, duties, rights, and confidential information, not honesty alone.
Arabic variations + translation: اِئْتَمَنَ (verb) — entrust; place in trust | أَمِين (adjective) — trustworthy; honest

Meaning: A binding pledge, entrusted obligation, or covenant. It can denote divine covenant, human commitment, or a duty whose breach is betrayal.
Arabic variations + translation: عَاهَدَ (verb) — make a covenant; pledge
Alternative context meaning(s): Historical context: era; reign or period.

Meaning: A solemn binding covenant, often witnessed before Allah. It is stronger than a contract; it carries sacred and moral accountability.
Comprehensive righteousness expressed through faith, worship, generosity, and good character. It is broader than a single charitable act.
Arabic variations + translation: بَرَّ (verb) — be dutiful; show kindness | بَارّ (active participle) — dutiful; righteous | أَبْرَار (plural) — the righteous; the dutiful
Alternative context meaning(s): Different vocalization (البَرّ): dry land; land as opposed to sea.

Meaning: A community united by a shared faith, purpose, or messenger; in sermons, usually the worldwide Muslim community. It is not identical to a nation-state or ethnicity.
Alternative context meaning(s): Qur'anic context: a period of time (12:45); elsewhere, an exemplary leader/model (16:120).

Meaning: The united Muslim community or a body gathered around legitimate guidance. The word can also simply mean a group, so theological claims depend on context.
Arabic variations + translation: جَمَعَ (verb) — gather; collect

Meaning: A bond of mutual loyalty, dignity, and responsibility grounded in faith or humanity. Ukhuwwah entails rights and duties, not emotional closeness alone.
The Islamic principle of consulting relevant people before making a responsible decision. It is not identical to a single modern political system or to majority voting in every matter.
Arabic variations + translation: شَاوَرَ (verb) — consult; seek counsel
Alternative context meaning(s): Institutional context: consultative council; advisory body.

Meaning: The resurrection and great standing of creation before Allah for judgment. The word emphasizes rising and standing, not only the destruction of the world.
Arabic variations + translation: قَامَ (verb) — rise; stand

Meaning: Allah's reckoning of beliefs, intentions, words, and deeds. It is moral accounting, not arithmetic alone.
Arabic variations + translation: حَاسَبَ (verb) — call to account; reckon | حَاسِب (noun) — accountant; reckoner

Meaning: The divinely just weighing of deeds, records, or people on the Day of Judgment. It expresses exact accountability and is treated in sermons as an eschatological reality.
Arabic variations + translation: وَزَنَ (verb) — weigh; measure by weight

Meaning: The straight path of guidance, and in eschatological contexts the crossing over Hell toward Paradise. The intended meaning depends on the passage.
Intercession granted only by Allah's permission and approval. It is not an automatic spiritual privilege or a means of overriding divine judgment.
Arabic variations + translation: شَفَعَ (verb) — intercede; mediate | شَافِع (noun) — intercessor; mediator

Meaning: The divinely prepared everlasting abode of nearness, safety, and reward. It is Paradise; the root image of a concealed garden does not exhaust the concept.
The divinely created abode or punishment of the condemned. It means Hell, not every physical flame.
Allah's enabling a person to choose, pursue, and accomplish what is right. It joins sound intention, ability, and successful action.
Arabic variations + translation: وَفَّقَ (verb) — enable; grant success | مُوَفَّق (adjective) — successful; well-guided

Meaning: Soundly directed judgment and conduct leading to a good end. It combines intellectual rightness, maturity, and practical direction.
Arabic variations + translation: رَشَدَ (verb) — be rightly guided; mature | رَاشِد (adjective) — mature; rightly guided
Alternative context meaning(s): Legal context: maturity and sound judgment sufficient to manage property.

Meaning: Detachment of the heart from excessive attachment to worldly things in favour of the Hereafter. It does not require poverty or abandoning lawful possessions.
Arabic variations + translation: زَهِدَ فِي (verb) — abstain from; be detached from | زَاهِد (noun/adjective) — ascetic; detached

Meaning: The Lord who creates, owns, sustains, governs, and nurtures creation. The word conveys comprehensive divine care and authority, not merely the social title "master.".
The being who is worshipped; in Islamic creed, Allah alone is rightfully worshipped. The concept concerns entitlement to worship, not power alone.
Exclusive divine right to worship. It is a creed term denoting that all worship belongs to Allah alone.
Allah's unique lordship over creation. It includes creating, owning, sustaining, decreeing, and governing all things.
A divine name expressing vast, all-encompassing mercy. Its intensive form conveys the abundance and breadth of Allah's mercy.
A divine name expressing continuing and specially bestowed mercy. It conveys enduring mercy rather than an ordinary kindly disposition.
Arabic variations + translation: رَحِمَ (verb) — have mercy; show compassion

Meaning: The Oft-Forgiving who repeatedly covers and pardons sin. It stresses abundance and recurrence of forgiveness.
Arabic variations + translation: غَفَرَ (verb) — forgive; pardon | غَافِر (active participle) — forgiver; forgiving

Meaning: The Constantly and Abundantly Forgiving. It is stronger than a one-time act of pardon; it conveys repeated forgiveness.
Arabic variations + translation: غَفَرَ (verb) — forgive; pardon | غَافِر (active participle) — forgiver; forgiving

Meaning: The divine name of the One who pardons and effaces sin. It can imply removal of blame and its trace, beyond withholding punishment.
Arabic variations + translation: عَفَا عَنْ (verb) — pardon; forgive

Meaning: The One who repeatedly turns to servants in mercy and accepts repentance. It means enabling and accepting repentance, not repenting Himself.
The divine name expressing especially tender and gentle mercy that relieves suffering.
Arabic variations + translation: رَأَفَ بِـ (verb) — show compassion; have pity

Meaning: The Loving and Beloved, whose love is active and beneficent. It is not sentiment alone but favour, nearness, and benevolence.
Arabic variations + translation: وَدَّ (verb) — love; wish

Meaning: The Subtly Kind and perfectly aware of hidden details. It combines subtle knowledge with unobtrusive kindness and providence.
Arabic variations + translation: لَطُفَ (verb) — be gentle; be subtle

Meaning: The One fully acquainted with inner realities and outcomes. It is not merely possessing information; it implies penetrating knowledge of what is hidden.
Arabic variations + translation: خَبِرَ (verb) — know by experience; be informed

Meaning: The All-Knowing without limit or acquisition. It denotes complete, timeless, and unfailing knowledge.
Arabic variations + translation: عَلِمَ (verb) — know; learn | عَالِم (noun/adjective) — scholar; knowledgeable

Meaning: The Perfectly Wise who places everything appropriately. It includes perfect judgment, purpose, and right placement, not cleverness alone.
The Forbearing who does not hasten punishment despite power. It is deliberate restraint, not inability or passivity.
Arabic variations + translation: حَلُمَ (verb) — be forbearing; be mild

Meaning: The divine name expressing supreme generosity, nobility, honour, and graciousness.
Arabic variations + translation: كَرُمَ (verb) — be noble; be generous

Meaning: The Most Generous and Most Noble. It carries both munificence and incomparable nobility.
Arabic variations + translation: كَرُمَ (verb) — be noble; be generous | كَرِيم (adjective) — noble; generous

Meaning: The Unceasing Bestower of gifts without compensation. It stresses free, repeated, undeserved bestowal.
Arabic variations + translation: وَهَبَ (verb) — give; grant | هِبَة (noun) — gift; grant

Meaning: The Constant Provider who creates and delivers all provision. It includes material, spiritual, lawful, and inward sustenance.
Arabic variations + translation: رَزَقَ (verb) — provide; sustain | رَازِق (active participle) — provider; sustainer

Meaning: The divine name meaning the Opener who grants relief, opens paths of mercy or victory, and judges decisively between parties. The intended emphasis depends on context.
Arabic variations + translation: فَتَحَ (verb) — open; grant victory | فَاتِح (active participle) — opener; conqueror

Meaning: The perfectly effective Helper who protects, supports, and grants victory.
Arabic variations + translation: نَصَرَ (verb) — help; grant victory | نَاصِر (noun) — helper; supporter

Meaning: The Protecting Patron and Ally who is near to His servants. The word can combine protection, authority, loyalty, and closeness, so "friend" is too weak.
Arabic variations + translation: وَلِيَ (verb) — be near; take charge | أَوْلِيَاء (plural) — allies; guardians
Alternative context meaning(s): Family/legal context: guardian; person with legal authority.

Meaning: The Patron, Master, Protector, or Ally. It is a relational term whose exact English rendering depends on who is speaking and the surrounding context.
Arabic variations + translation: مَوَالٍ (plural) — patrons; clients

Meaning: The fully sufficient Trustee upon whom all affairs may be entrusted. In contexts of reliance on Allah, it means the One who manages matters perfectly.
Arabic variations + translation: وَكَلَ (verb) — entrust; appoint

Meaning: The Perfect Preserver and Watchful Guardian. It includes guarding, preserving, recording, and preventing loss.
Arabic variations + translation: حَفِظَ (verb) — preserve; protect | حَافِظ (active participle) — guardian; memorizer

Meaning: The Ever-Watchful Observer from whom nothing is absent. It conveys continuous, morally consequential oversight, not surveillance alone.
Arabic variations + translation: رَقَبَ (verb) — watch; observe

Meaning: The One who is fully sufficient for His servants and who reckons all deeds exactly. Both meanings are used in religious language.
Alternative context meaning(s): Social/classical context: person of noble lineage; person of standing.

Meaning: The ever-present Witness whose knowledge misses nothing. As a divine name, it does not mean a person killed as a martyr.
Arabic variations + translation: شَهِدَ (verb) — witness; testify | شَاهِد (noun) — witness; observer

Meaning: The Sustainer who apportions nourishment and preserves creation, with complete power over it. The word has a wider sense than "feeder.".
The One whose power and ability are complete and unrestricted. Divine power is fully effective, not merely potential.
Arabic variations + translation: قَدَرَ عَلَى (verb) — be able; have power | قَادِر (adjective) — capable; powerful

Meaning: The All-Powerful who determines and effects all things. It is an intensive divine attribute of comprehensive power.
Arabic variations + translation: قَدَرَ عَلَى (verb) — be able; have power | قَادِر (adjective) — capable; powerful

Meaning: The Supremely Powerful whose power is manifest and irresistible. It emphasizes exercised and overwhelming power.
Arabic variations + translation: اِقْتَدَرَ عَلَى (verb) — have power; be capable

Meaning: The Perfectly Strong, untouched by weakness. It is absolute and not bodily.
Arabic variations + translation: قَوِيَ (verb) — be strong; grow strong

Meaning: The Firm and Unfailing in strength. It conveys unbreakable, inexhaustible power rather than physical hardness.
The Irresistible One whose authority cannot be overcome and who restores what is broken. As a divine name, it does not mean an unjust tyrant.
Arabic variations + translation: جَبَرَ (verb) — mend; compel | جَابِر (active participle) — one who mends; consoler

Meaning: The Supremely Great, exalted above every defect and rival. Arrogant pride is blameworthy in creatures, whereas this divine name expresses rightful greatness and transcendence.
Arabic variations + translation: تَكَبَّرَ (verb) — act arrogantly; exalt oneself

Meaning: The Incomparably Great in essence, rank, and authority. It does not refer to physical size; it denotes absolute greatness.
Arabic variations + translation: كَبُرَ (verb) — be great; grow large

Meaning: The Tremendously Magnificent and worthy of awe. It carries a stronger sacred sense than the ordinary word "great.".
Arabic variations + translation: عَظُمَ (verb) — be great; be immense

Meaning: The Most High in rank, authority, and transcendence. It does not refer only to spatial height; it denotes exaltedness above all imperfection.
Arabic variations + translation: عَلَا (verb) — rise; be exalted | عَالٍ (adjective) — high; elevated

Meaning: The Supremely Exalted above all limitation and false attribution. An intensive expression of transcendence.
Arabic variations + translation: تَعَالَى (verb) — be exalted; rise above | مُتَعَالٍ (adjective) — exalted; lofty

Meaning: The Absolutely Pure and Holy, exalted above every defect and creaturely limitation. "Holy" is only an approximate English equivalent.
Arabic variations + translation: قُدْس (noun) — holiness; sanctity | مُقَدَّس (adjective) — holy; sacred

Meaning: The One free from every defect and the source of safety and peace. As a divine name, it means more than tranquillity.
Arabic variations + translation: سَلِمَ (verb) — be safe; be sound
Alternative context meaning(s): Everyday usage: greeting of peace; salutation.

Meaning: The Giver of security and the One who confirms truth. As a divine name, it does not mean "a believer.".
Arabic variations + translation: أَمِنَ (verb) — be safe; feel secure | آمَنَ (verb) — believe; have faith

Meaning: The Supreme Overseer, Guardian, and Witness whose authority and knowledge encompass all things.
Arabic variations + translation: هَيْمَنَ عَلَى (verb) — oversee; dominate

Meaning: The One without partner in divinity. It is not merely numerical oneness; it denies any partner or division in worship and lordship.
Arabic variations + translation: وَحْدَة (noun) — unity; unit

Meaning: The Uniquely One, indivisible and without equal. In creed, it expresses absolute uniqueness rather than numerical oneness alone.
The Self-Sufficient Master upon whom all creation depends. No single English word fully captures both perfect independence and universal dependence upon Him.
A divinely grounded religious way or confessional tradition. It denotes the inherited or followed way of faith, especially the creed of Abraham.
A binding responsibility, legal liability, or protected covenantal status. The exact sense can be obligation, protection, or guarantee depending on context.
Faithful allegiance, protective loyalty, and committed solidarity. Its theological and communal sense is stronger and more relational than preference.
Disavowal of false worship and principled separation from wrongdoing. It does not simply mean personal innocence.
Perverse misdirection chosen in opposition to sound guidance. It implies morally blameworthy deviation, not innocent confusion.
Anything worshipped, obeyed, or followed in rebellion against Allah's authority and limits. It can refer to a false deity, satanic authority, tyrannical power, or a claimant to divine rights.
A broad Qur'anic term for false objects of worship, superstition, sorcery, or other forms of religious falsehood. Its exact referent depends on context.
Rivals set up as equals or counterparts to Allah. It stresses treating created things as peers in love, obedience, or worship.
Intercessors whose mediation is sought or granted. Intercession in Islamic theology is dependent on Allah's permission, not independent influence.
Being charged by divine law with accountable duties. It signifies morally binding religious responsibility, not merely a task.
Arabic variations + translation: كَلَّفَ (verb) — assign; impose a duty | مُكَلَّف (passive participle) — legally responsible; assigned

Meaning: Certainty reached through reliable knowledge, evidence, or report. It is the first of three Qur'anic expressions describing degrees or modes of certainty.
Certainty comparable to direct seeing. It describes immediate experiential confirmation, not a literal "eye" belonging to certainty.
Certainty fully realized through direct encounter with reality. It is the most complete expression in the Qur'anic sequence of certainty.
Testimony or witnessing; it can also mean the visible, perceptible realm. Context may refer to legal evidence, the confession of faith, martyrdom, or the world of direct perception.
Arabic variations + translation: شَهِدَ (verb) — witness; testify | شَاهِد (noun) — witness; observer

Meaning: Declaring Allah free of every defect and creaturely limitation. It is a theological act of transcendence, not praise in general.
Arabic variations + translation: نَزَّهَ (verb) — declare free from; exalt above imperfection | مُنَزَّه (adjective) — free from imperfection; transcendent

Meaning: Likening divine attributes to created qualities. It denotes anthropomorphic assimilation, not every analogy.
Arabic variations + translation: شَبَّهَ (verb) — compare; liken | مُشَبِّه (active participle) — one who likens; comparer

Meaning: Denying, emptying, or suspending the meanings of divine attributes. A technical theological term, not ordinary interruption.
Arabic variations + translation: عَطَّلَ (verb) — suspend; disable | مُعَطِّل (active participle) — one who suspends; negator

Meaning: The sending down of revelation in stages and with divine authority. It highlights descent from Allah and often gradual delivery.
Arabic variations + translation: نَزَّلَ (verb) — send down; reveal | مُنَزَّل (passive participle) — sent down; revealed

Meaning: The divine criterion that separates truth from falsehood. It can name the Qur'an or any decisive divine distinction.
Guidance that directs toward truth and a sound end. It refers to revelation or divine enabling, not information alone.
Clear proofs or insights that illuminate spiritual and moral truth. The plural refers to inward perception and evidence, not physical eyesight.
A text whose meaning or ruling is firmly established and relatively clear. In Qur'anic studies, definitions vary according to the way it is contrasted with mutashabih.
Alternative context meaning(s): Ordinary descriptive context: firmly constructed; well-made.

Meaning: A text whose exact meaning, application, or ultimate referent is not immediately decisive. It may require interpretation or humble suspension of judgment and is not necessarily contradictory.
A later ruling or text that replaces the operative legal ruling of an earlier one. The concept concerns legal effect, not denial of the earlier revelation.
A ruling whose operative legal force has been replaced by a later ruling. The earlier verse or report remains part of revelation or transmission even when its ruling no longer applies.
Measured, clear, and deliberate recitation of the Qur'an. It emphasizes correct articulation, pacing, and reflection rather than musical performance.
Arabic variations + translation: رَتَّلَ (verb) — recite distinctly; recite measuredly | مُرَتِّل (noun) — measured reciter; reciter

Meaning: Reciting the Qur'an while giving each letter and recitation rule its proper pronunciation. It concerns disciplined phonetic accuracy, not ornamentation alone.
Arabic variations + translation: جَوَّدَ (verb) — perfect; improve | مُجَوِّد (noun) — skilled reciter; practitioner of tajwid

Meaning: In the expression "seven ahruf," a technical term for divinely permitted modes of early Qur'anic recitation. Scholars differ about their precise nature, but the word does not mean seven alphabet letters or the seven canonical readings.
The inherited consonantal spelling and written form of the Qur'anic codex. It is a technical term for orthography, not drawing.
A physical written codex containing the Qur'anic text. It is the written copy, whereas the Qur'an is the revealed recitation and message.
The chain through which a report or recitation is attributed to its source. It is a formal transmission chain, not "support" in the general sense.
Arabic variations + translation: أَسْنَدَ (verb) — attribute; support | مُسْنَد (passive participle/noun) — attributed; supported

Meaning: A transmitted report, narration, or version received through a chain. In Qur'anic recitation, it can mean a formally transmitted recension associated with a reader.
Knowledge based on sound evidence and understanding. In religious sermons, it often refers to sacred or beneficial knowledge rather than modern science specifically.
Arabic variations + translation: عَلِمَ (verb) — know; learn | عَالِم (noun/adjective) — scholar; knowledgeable

Meaning: A moral lesson drawn by moving from an event or sign to its deeper meaning. It is more than an example.
Reflective inference that draws a lesson from signs, history, or outcomes. It is not mere attention; it involves moral and analogical reasoning.
Arabic variations + translation: اِعْتَبَرَ (verb) — consider; take into account | مُعْتَبَر (adjective) — recognized; valid

Meaning: Discernment that reads outward signs with trained inward perception. In ethical discourse, it is perceptiveness rather than fortune-telling or certainty about the unseen.
Alternative context meaning(s): Classical descriptive context: physiognomy; inference from outward signs.

Meaning: Careful verification before accepting or acting on information. It means checking truth and avoiding haste, especially regarding reports.
Seeking and attaining clarity through verification. In a command, it means to investigate carefully rather than merely notice.
Issuing a reasoned religious legal answer to a particular question. It is nonjudicial guidance based on recognized legal method.
Arabic variations + translation: أَفْتَى (verb) — issue a legal opinion; give a fatwa | مُفْتٍ (noun) — mufti; legal scholar

Meaning: Authoritative transmission of text or report. It contrasts with pure reasoning and refers to transmitted evidence.
Reasoning from evidence to a warranted conclusion. A technical scholarly process, not rhetorical persuasion.
Arabic variations + translation: اِسْتَدَلَّ (verb) — infer; adduce evidence | مُسْتَدِلّ (active participle) — reasoner; one adducing evidence

Meaning: A person who sincerely affirms and confirms the truth. In faith contexts, the word suggests inward acceptance that leads to truthful response.
A person who protects themselves from Allah's displeasure through vigilant obedience and avoidance of sin. "Pious" is only a partial equivalent.
A God-oriented scholar and educator who combines knowledge, wisdom, and gradual spiritual formation of others.
A person humbly settled, tranquil, and receptive before Allah. It combines lowliness, trust, and willing obedience.
One who repeatedly returns to Allah in repentance and devotion. It suggests frequent, heartfelt returning, not a single apology.
One who turns back to Allah with reliance and obedient devotion. It is a sustained orientation toward Allah.
One who actively remembers and mentions Allah. It includes heart, tongue, awareness, and obedience.
One who relies upon Allah while taking legitimate means. It combines heart-reliance with responsible action.
Continual turning of the heart and conduct back to Allah. It is broader than repentance from a specific sin and describes an enduring devotional orientation.
Humble, tranquil submission and inward settling before Allah. The word evokes low, stable ground as an image of a settled heart.
Arabic variations + translation: أَخْبَتَ (verb) — humble oneself; submit | مُخْبِت (adjective) — humble; devout

Meaning: Living with sustained awareness that Allah observes and knows all things. It is a spiritual practice of accountability, not surveillance of other people.
Arabic variations + translation: رَاقَبَ (verb) — watch; observe | مُرَاقِب (noun/adjective) — observer; watchful

Meaning: Examining and holding oneself accountable before final judgment. It means moral self-audit, not bookkeeping.
Arabic variations + translation: حَاسَبَ (verb) — hold accountable; audit | مُحَاسِب (noun) — accountant; auditor

Meaning: Disciplined striving against the ego, habits, and obstacles to obedience. In this context it commonly means inner moral struggle, not armed conflict.
Arabic variations + translation: جَاهَدَ (verb) — strive; struggle | مُجَاهِد (active participle) — one who strives; struggler

Meaning: Conscious recognition of one's complete need of Allah. It is spiritual and existential dependence, not merely financial poverty.
Arabic variations + translation: اِفْتَقَرَ إِلَى (verb) — be in need of; lack | مُفْتَقِر (adjective) — needy; dependent

Meaning: Spiritual nearness to Allah through His favour, worship, and obedience. It does not imply physical distance or bodily location.
Intimate spiritual ease and comfort found in remembering and worshipping Allah. It is inward familiarity with devotion, not sociability.
A prescribed act of devotion, especially sacrificial or pilgrimage worship. It can denote worship generally or a specific sacrificial rite.
A divinely appointed symbol or rite that publicly marks devotion. It is a sacred sign whose honour reflects reverence for Allah.
Alternative context meaning(s): General lexical context: distinguishing sign; marker.

Meaning: The divinely established rites and symbols of worship. It carries sacred legal significance, not cultural pageantry.
Prolonged devout obedience, standing, or supplication. Its exact meaning varies between Qur'anic passages and legal discussions.
The odd-numbered night prayer concluding voluntary worship. A technical devotional term, not arithmetic alone.
Alternative context meaning(s): Anatomy/music context: tendon; string or cord.

Meaning: Ramadan night prayers performed with intervals of rest. The name reflects pauses between units, not relaxation as the purpose.
Recommended Prophetic practices or established normative ways. In other contexts, the plural can also refer to recurring patterns or laws established by Allah.
A voluntary act of worship beyond what is obligatory. It is spiritually meritorious and can repair deficiencies in obligatory worship.
Alternative context meaning(s): Classical/Qur'anic context: additional gift; something beyond what is due.

Meaning: A specifically apportioned and binding religious obligation. It is legally mandatory and divinely assigned.
An integral element without which an act of worship is invalid. It is an internal essential component, not merely something important.
Acts that invalidate worship or a legal transaction. These are technically defined nullifiers, not anything disliked.
An act religiously discouraged but not normally forbidden. The English word "hated" is too emotional for this technical legal category.
An act that is legally permitted in itself, without inherent reward or sin. Intention and consequences can change its moral value.
A matter whose lawful or unlawful status is not sufficiently clear. It calls for verification and caution, not suspicion toward people.
Ritual impurity defined by Islamic law. It is a juridical category, not general uncleanliness.
A state of minor or major ritual impurity that prevents certain acts of worship until purification. In Islamic law, it does not mean an ordinary event.
Ritual purification with clean earth or dust when water is unavailable or cannot safely be used. It is a legally defined substitute, not ordinary "dry washing.".
Cleansing oneself after relieving oneself. It is a technical practice of ritual cleanliness, not general bathing.
Arabic variations + translation: اِسْتَنْجَى (verb) — cleanse after relieving oneself

Meaning: Cleansing after relieving oneself with suitable dry material. Stones were historically common, but equivalent clean materials may fulfil the function.
Arabic variations + translation: اِسْتَجْمَرَ (verb) — cleanse with dry material; cleanse with stones

Meaning: The direction of the Kaaba faced during prayer. Without vowel marks, the word can be confused with a homograph meaning "kiss.".
Arabic variations + translation: قِبْلِيّ (nisba adjective) — qibla-related; southern
Alternative context meaning(s): General figurative context: focus/destination; direction toward which people turn.

Meaning: Attentive awareness of Allah and the act of worship within the heart. It describes inward presence rather than concentration alone.
Declaring "Allah is greater" as an act of glorification, especially by saying "Allahu akbar.".
Arabic variations + translation: كَبَّرَ (verb) — magnify; say 'Allahu akbar'

Meaning: Praising Allah, especially by saying "al-hamdu lillah." The term often names this established formula of praise.
Arabic variations + translation: حَمَّدَ (verb) — praise; say 'alhamdulillah'

Meaning: Declaring Allah free from every defect and limitation. It is more specific than general praise.
Arabic variations + translation: سَبَّحَ (verb) — glorify; declare free of imperfection | مُسَبِّح (active participle) — one who glorifies; praising

Meaning: Saying "there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah." The term names this declaration of divine oneness, not chanting in general.
Arabic variations + translation: هَلَّلَ (verb) — say 'la ilaha illa Allah'; acclaim

Meaning: Saying "there is no power or ability except through Allah." The formula acknowledges that all effective strength and change depend on Him.
Saying "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs," or a related formula of reliance. The word is a devotional abbreviation, not calculation.
Seeking Allah's protection from evil. It is a worshipful appeal, commonly before recitation.
Saying "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful." The word is the technical name for beginning with this formula.
Saying "All praise belongs to Allah." The word is a coined name for this formula, not praise in general.
The shorter call immediately preceding congregational prayer. The same Arabic form has unrelated everyday meanings.
Leadership of congregational prayer; more broadly, leadership, authority, or exemplary guidance. The intended meaning can differ significantly across legal, political, and theological contexts.
Following the prayer leader's actions in proper sequence. In congregational prayer it is a technical relationship to the imam.
Arabic variations + translation: اِقْتَدَى بِـ (verb) — follow; emulate | مُقْتَدٍ (active participle) — follower; imitator

Meaning: Joining and following an imam in congregational prayer. It is a technical prayer term governing how the follower coordinates with the imam.
Arabic variations + translation: اِئْتَمَّ بِـ (verb) — follow an imam in prayer | مُؤْتَمّ (active participle) — follower in prayer

Meaning: The formal sermon delivered as part of Friday or Eid worship. It has ritual and legal features beyond ordinary public speaking.
Arabic variations + translation: خَطَبَ (verb) — preach; address | خَطِيب (noun) — preacher; orator
Alternative context meaning(s): Different vocalization (الخِطْبَة): marriage proposal; engagement request.

Meaning: Devotional seclusion in a mosque with intention of worship. It is a regulated religious practice, not a wellness retreat.
Arabic variations + translation: اِعْتَكَفَ (verb) — remain in retreat; seclude oneself for worship | مُعْتَكِف (noun) — person in retreat; one in i'tikaf

Meaning: Ending a fast at its lawful time; also not fasting when permitted. The common English sense can obscure the religious act.
Arabic variations + translation: أَفْطَرَ (verb) — break a fast; cease fasting | مُفْطِر (active participle) — one breaking the fast; not fasting

Meaning: The pre-dawn meal eaten before a day of fasting. It is a recommended Prophetic practice, not simply a late-night meal.
Entering the consecrated state for Hajj or Umrah through intention and prescribed restrictions. The familiar garments mark this state but are not the state itself.
Arabic variations + translation: أَحْرَمَ (verb) — enter ritual consecration; assume ihram | مُحْرِم (noun/adjective) — pilgrim in ihram; ritually consecrated

Meaning: The ritual walking between Safa and Marwah during Hajj or Umrah. Outside pilgrimage, the same word commonly means effort or striving.
Being present at Arafah during the prescribed pilgrimage time, an essential rite of Hajj. Continuous physical standing is not required.
Casting pebbles at the designated pillars during Hajj. The targets symbolize rejection of temptation; they are not literally Satan.
An animal offering designated for Hajj or Umrah. Without vowel marks, the word can be confused with another word meaning guidance.
Alternative context meaning(s): General lexical context: manner of conduct; way or practice.

Meaning: The sacrificial animal offered during Eid al-Adha according to prescribed rules. It is a devotional offering, not a "victim.".
The animal sacrifice offered in gratitude for a newborn, commonly accompanied by naming and other practices. The term is not simply hair cutting.
Alternative context meaning(s): Classical lexical context: a newborn's first hair; hair present at birth.

Meaning: Completely sincere and reforming, especially in the expression "sincere repentance." It describes repentance free of deception and accompanied by genuine correction.
Immediate cessation and abandonment of a sin. In repentance language it means stopping the offence, not gradual reduction.
Arabic variations + translation: أَقْلَعَ عَنْ (verb) — cease; quit

Meaning: Expiation or removal of sins; in another context, declaring a person to be an unbeliever. The surrounding words are essential because the two meanings are very different.
Arabic variations + translation: كَفَّرَ (verb) — expiate; declare an unbeliever

Meaning: A prescribed act of expiation for a specific violation. It does not necessarily replace repentance, compensation, or restoration of another person's rights.
Established formulas and acts of remembering Allah for recurring times and situations. They include praise, supplication, and Qur'anic phrases.
The pilgrimage response beginning "Labbayka," expressing readiness, obedience, and repeated response to Allah's call.
Arabic variations + translation: لَبَّى (verb) — answer; recite the talbiyah | مُلَبٍّ (active participle) — one reciting the talbiyah; respondent

Meaning: Seeking urgent rescue or relief. In theological discussion, the meaning and ruling depend on whom help is sought from and what ability is attributed to them.
Seeking reinforcement, support, or aid. Because the word can be used materially or spiritually, the source and kind of help must be clear from context.
Arabic variations + translation: اِسْتَمَدَّ مِن (verb) — derive from; seek support from | مُسْتَمَدّ (passive participle) — derived; drawn from

Meaning: A request or question. In devotional context, it can mean asking Allah for a need; in scholarly context, it means an issue under discussion.
Intimate, private conversation and supplication directed to Allah. It conveys closeness, confidentiality, and inward address.
Arabic variations + translation: نَاجَى (verb) — confide privately; speak intimately to | مُنَاجٍ (active participle) — one confiding; intimate speaker

Meaning: Humble submission and loweredness before Allah, especially during hardship. It is voluntary spiritual yielding, not degradation before people.
Humble, broken-hearted pleading before Allah. It denotes spiritually truthful need, not degrading performance.
Contrite humility and awareness of need before Allah. It is not psychological collapse or loss of human dignity.
Arabic variations + translation: اِنْكَسَرَ (verb) — break; become broken | مُنْكَسِر (adjective) — broken; humbled

Meaning: Hopeful desire directed toward Allah. It is often paired with awe-filled fear to express balance between hope and fear.
Awe-filled fear that turns a person away from disobedience. It is devotional reverence, not panic.
Entrusting the result of one's affairs to Allah after responsible effort. It is inward surrender, not abandonment of action.
Arabic variations + translation: فَوَّضَ (verb) — delegate; entrust | مُفَوَّض (noun/adjective) — delegate; authorized

Meaning: Settled confidence in Allah's promise, wisdom, and care. The word itself can mean trust generally, so its object must be clear.
Expecting Allah's mercy, wisdom, and good treatment while continuing repentance and obedience. It is not presumption that actions have no consequences.
Unfounded negative suspicion about Allah or other people. It can concern divine wisdom, another person's motives, or social conduct and must be understood from context.
Private conversation or secret counsel. Qur'anic usage can refer positively to intimate supplication or negatively to concealed plotting.
A legitimate means of drawing nearer to Allah. The term names the means itself and does not automatically specify a disputed form of intercession.
Seeking nearness to Allah or an answer to prayer through a recognized means. Jurists differ about some forms, so the specific means must be identified.
Forbearing self-control when one has the power to retaliate. Without context, the same spelling can also mean a dream.
Deliberate composure that avoids rash action. It is thoughtful restraint, not laziness or indecision.
Honourable character and socially recognized decency that protect human dignity. Although often translated "manliness," the ethical quality is not limited to men.
Outlasting opposition through greater steadfastness. It implies competing in endurance, not merely waiting.
Arabic variations + translation: صَابَرَ (verb) — vie in endurance; endure against | مُصَابِر (active participle) — persevering; steadfast

Meaning: Sustained vigilance and readiness in defence of duty. In Qur'anic and devotional usage, it may refer either to frontier service or disciplined spiritual watchfulness.
Arabic variations + translation: رَابَطَ (verb) — remain stationed; keep watch | مُرَابِط (noun) — sentry; one stationed on guard

Meaning: Dignified modesty in appearance, speech, and social conduct. It denotes protected dignity rather than shame toward the body or ordinary interaction.
Arabic variations + translation: اِحْتَشَمَ (verb) — be modest; be decorous | مُحْتَشِم (adjective) — modest; decorous

Meaning: Gentle and accessible humility toward those under one's care. The expression is a Qur'anic image of tenderness, like a bird lowering its wing.
Guarding speech from falsehood, injury, and useless excess. It is a comprehensive discipline of verbal accountability.
Pausing long enough for judgment and action to mature. It is disciplined deliberation, not fear-driven indecision.
Concealing a person's non-public fault while encouraging correction and avoiding scandal. It does not justify hiding ongoing abuse, public danger, or violations of others' rights.
Courteous accommodation used to prevent harm while preserving principle. It differs from compromising truth merely to gain approval.
Arabic variations + translation: دَارَى (verb) — deal tactfully; conciliate | مُدَارٍ (active participle) — tactful; conciliatory

Meaning: Wisely overlooking minor faults that one has noticed. It does not mean ignoring serious harm or neglecting responsibility.
Arabic variations + translation: تَغَافَلَ (verb) — deliberately overlook; pretend not to notice | مُتَغَافِل (active participle) — deliberately overlooking; feigning ignorance

Meaning: Refraining from deserved personal retaliation despite having power. The expression praises moral strength, while public rights may still require justice.
Containing anger so it does not govern speech or action. It means mastery and redirection, not denial of emotion or tolerated abuse.
Restoring sound relations between estranged people. It is a major communal duty involving truth, justice, and reconciliation.
Meeting people with an open, pleasant, and approachable expression. It is a classical idiom and should not be translated literally as "a loose face.".
Giving urgent help to a person in acute distress. The expression conveys both urgency and moral responsibility.
Removing or easing another person's severe distress. The Prophetic expression connects relieving people in this life with receiving divine relief in the Hereafter.
Helping people meet legitimate and pressing needs. The word refers to needs and affairs, not every personal desire.
Supporting a dependent, burdened, or incapable person who cannot manage alone. It is a classical expression and does not mean carrying everyone physically.
Empowering and assisting those with limited power or capacity. It may be social, financial, physical, or situational; the phrase need not demean.
Supporting the wronged person in recovering safety and rights. It is effective advocacy and protection, not military victory.
Restoring wrongfully taken rights to their owners. It means violated rights or wrongful exactions, not abstract injustices.
Fulfilling the claims and obligations owed to Allah and to people. A right held by one person becomes a duty upon the person who owes it.
Honouring the persons, rights, times, places, and limits made inviolable by Allah. It is broader than respecting sacred objects.
Honouring the visible rites and symbols designated by Allah. It means reverent observance, not enlarging or idolizing symbols.
A heart free of rancour, envy, and malicious intent toward others. The expression is an idiom for inward moral soundness, not physical chest safety.
Inward clarity unclouded by persistent malice, vanity, or duplicity. It does not imply sinlessness; it describes cultivated moral lucidity.
Cleansing inward motives and states from spiritual corruption. It concerns intention and character, not ritual purification.
The recognized excellences of stable moral character. It points to embodied virtues rather than abstract moral theories.
The highest and most noble forms of moral character. It denotes elevated excellences, not generosity alone.
Removing excessive hardship recognized by Islamic law. Here, "haraj" means serious constriction, not social embarrassment.
A just, balanced, and morally excellent religious orientation. It does not mean compromise between truth and falsehood.
Sustainable and measured devotion without negligence or self-destructive excess. It expresses the Prophetic ideal of steady worship within human capacity.
Using available periods as opportunities for worship and benefit. It implies valuing a fleeting opportunity, not exploitation.
The juristic method of weighing competing benefits and harms when they cannot all be achieved or avoided. It is more than ordinary compromise.
Wishing to receive a blessing similar to another person's without wanting their blessing removed. It is positive emulation, not envy.
Deep concealed rancour or treacherous resentment. It denotes hidden hostility that contaminates relationships.
A grave fabricated falsehood that reverses or distorts reality. It is often used for calumny.
Attacking another's honour, lineage, integrity, or standing. In moral discourse it is verbal or reputational assault.
Treating truth, religion, or people as objects of derisive scorn. It conveys contempt and can be doctrinally grave when directed at sacred matters.
Arabic variations + translation: اِسْتَهْزَأَ بِـ (verb) — mock; ridicule | مُسْتَهْزِئ (noun/adjective) — mocker; ridiculing

Meaning: Calling one another by offensive labels or nicknames. It highlights a culture of exchanged humiliation.
Arabic variations + translation: تَنَابَزَ (verb) — exchange offensive nicknames; trade insults

Meaning: Breaking a solemn promise or covenant after confirming it. It evokes unravelling something firmly twisted.
Denying or covering over gratitude for a blessing. Depending on context, the word can mean ingratitude and may also be connected with disbelief.
Arrogant exultation in blessings that leads to ingratitude and wrongdoing. It condemns corrupted enjoyment, not happiness itself.
Arrogant, heedless exuberance produced by prosperity. It describes morally intoxicated self-indulgence, not ordinary cheerfulness.
Exceeding proper limits in spending, consumption, behaviour, or even otherwise lawful activity. It is broader than wasting money.
Arabic variations + translation: أَسْرَفَ (verb) — be excessive; squander | مُسْرِف (adjective) — wasteful; extravagant

Meaning: Possessive greed combining stinginess with an urge to acquire what others have. It is stronger than ordinary reluctance to spend.
Intense eagerness to acquire or retain something. The word can praise diligence, but in moral warnings it often means grasping attachment.
Secretly misappropriating communal, entrusted, or public property. The term has a strong religious association with betrayal of public trust and war gains.
Illicit gain that morally corrupts or destroys the person who consumes it. It includes bribery, extortion, and other unlawful earnings.
Wrongfully taking, using, or benefiting from other people's wealth. "Eating" is a Qur'anic idiom for unjust appropriation.
Culpably delaying payment of a due debt despite ability. It is a specific financial injustice, not general delay.
Giving less than what is due in weight, measure, quality, or rights. The Qur'anic warning extends beyond marketplace scales to any unfair shortchanging.
Arabic variations + translation: طَفَّفَ (verb) — give short measure; defraud in measure | مُطَفِّف (noun) — short-measurer; defrauder

Meaning: Concealing a relevant defect or creating a misleading impression in a transaction or transmitted report. Its specific technical meaning depends on whether the context is law, commerce, or hadith.
Arabic variations + translation: دَلَّسَ (verb) — conceal defects; misrepresent | مُدَلِّس (noun) — concealer; practitioner of tadlis

Meaning: Secretly arranging an outcome through means the other party does not perceive. When attributed to Allah, it denotes His decisive response to wrongful plotting, not moral deceit.
Purposeful hidden strategizing to overcome or harm an opponent. It can be defensive or blameworthy depending on agent and context.
Sins that people dismiss as insignificant even though their accumulation can be destructive. The word criticizes the person's minimization of them.

Displaying adornment or bodily attractions in a conspicuous way prohibited by Islamic modesty norms. The precise application depends on legal and social context and is not identical to ordinary grooming.

Seclusion between adults of opposite sexes who are legally marriageable to one another, in circumstances where normal public access or oversight is absent. It is a technical legal setting, not every form of privacy.
Accusing a chaste person of unlawful sexual intercourse without the legally required proof. It is a specific major offence, not every form of defamation.
Gambling or games of chance in which wealth is transferred through uncertain gain and loss. It does not include every competition or ordinary business risk.
Treating an omen as an independent cause for good or bad action. It is specifically omen-based pessimism that alters decisions.
The omen or superstitious foreboding itself. Its root arose from birds, but the concept covers many supposed signs.
Partisan loyalty that supports one's tribe or group even when it is unjust. The condemnation concerns loyalty overriding truth, not group identity itself.
A condition of ignorance, arrogance, and lawlessness opposed to divine guidance. It can describe recurring moral patterns, not only Arabia before Islam.
Wrongful transgression, oppression, or pursuit of superiority. In legal and political contexts, it can also refer to rebellion, so the surrounding context matters.
A Qur'anic image of rust or covering formed on the heart through accumulated sin. It describes loss of spiritual receptivity, not a physical substance.
A Qur'anic image of the heart becoming unreceptive after persistent rejection. It describes a consequence of culpable refusal, not literal printing.
A Qur'anic image of the heart being sealed against guidance after persistent rejection. It is a grave spiritual condition, not a medical description.
Spiritual hardness that makes reminders and suffering fail to awaken mercy. It is a cultivated moral state, not an immutable personality trait.
The heart's loss of spiritual awareness and responsiveness. A metaphor for moral-spiritual lifelessness, not bodily death.
Personal desire treated as an authority against truth and duty. The word does not condemn every desire, only desire followed in opposition to guidance.
Allowing appetites to direct conduct without lawful restraint. The criticism targets domination by desire, not human appetite itself.
Prolonged worldly expectation that delays repentance and useful action. It means living as though death and accountability were remote, not healthy hope.
Deliberately turning away from truth or reminder after it reaches a person. It is active disengagement, not simple distraction or lack of exposure.
Arabic variations + translation: أَعْرَضَ عَنْ (verb) — turn away; disregard | مُعْرِض (active participle) — one who turns away; dismissive

Meaning: Diversion that occupies a person away from what deserves greater priority. Its moral value depends on what it distracts from, not amusement alone.
Acting or enduring hardship while consciously seeking reward from Allah. Intention transforms ordinary service or suffering into an act of worship.
Arabic variations + translation: اِحْتَسَبَ (verb) — seek reward; reckon | مُحْتَسِب (noun) — one seeking reward; market inspector

Meaning: A test from Allah that reveals, educates, and distinguishes people's responses. It can occur through prosperity as well as adversity.
Arabic variations + translation: اِبْتَلَى (verb) — test; try | مُبْتَلًى (passive participle) — tested; afflicted

Meaning: A severe ordeal that examines and exposes steadfastness. It implies prolonged pressure, including persecution.
Alternative context meaning(s): Historical context: al-Miḥna, the Abbasid-era theological inquisition.

Meaning: Adversity involving pain, harm, or material constriction. It is commonly paired with prosperity and ease.
Prosperity and ease that can themselves test gratitude and character. It describes favourable circumstances, not happiness alone.
Severe deprivation, poverty, or distress that presses upon life. It emphasizes material hardship.
Relief and opening granted by Allah after severe constriction. The phrase nurtures hope without guaranteeing a particular worldly result or timetable.
Hopeful confidence in Allah's wisdom, mercy, and fulfilment of His promise. It coexists with repentance and effort; it is not presumption of immunity from consequences.
Accepting Allah's decree without inward rebellion while continuing lawful action. It does not require liking pain, refusing treatment, or abandoning efforts at improvement.
Trustfully yielding one's judgment and will to established divine guidance. It is conscious submission, not unthinking passivity.
Arabic variations + translation: سَلَّمَ (verb) — hand over; submit

Meaning: Using lawful practical causes and means while relying on Allah for the outcome. It rejects both fatalism and belief that causes operate independently of Him.
Neglecting effort while falsely claiming reliance on Allah. It is the blameworthy opposite or counterfeit of genuine reliance.
Arabic variations + translation: تَوَاكَلَ (verb) — rely passively on others; shirk effort | مُتَوَاكِل (adjective) — passively dependent; indolent

Meaning: Sustained struggle to govern desire, anger, habit, and ego according to divine guidance. It is inner moral discipline, not violence against oneself.
An inward opening granted by Allah that produces receptivity, courage, and ease in carrying truth. It is a Qur'anic idiom, not a medical procedure.
Inner constriction expressed as distress, reluctance, or difficulty bearing a matter. It may be spiritual or emotional and should not automatically be treated as a medical diagnosis.
Allah's strengthening and steadying a frightened or grieving heart. It is a Qur'anic image of stabilizing courage and certainty.
Strengthening the heart so it remains coherent and steadfast under intense emotional pressure. The expression emphasizes stabilization of the deeply affected inner self.
Comforting and restoring the dignity of a person whose inner state has been wounded. It is a common idiom for consoling the broken-hearted.
Humble contrition before Allah arising from awareness of need and fault. It is spiritually valued dependence, not abuse, despair, or damaged self-worth.
Recognizing one's complete need of Allah for existence, guidance, and ability. The poverty described is spiritual and existential, not financial.
False confidence that one is safe from Allah's judgment while persisting in sin. The phrase condemns presumption, not hopeful trust in divine mercy.
Advance warning that allows a person to avoid danger or punishment. In prophetic teaching, warning is a form of mercy because it precedes consequences.
Purifying the soul while cultivating and increasing virtue. The word combines cleansing and growth, not ritual washing.
Arabic variations + translation: زَكَّى (verb) — purify; attest good character | مُزَكٍّ (noun) — purifier; character witness

Meaning: Faithful and complete delivery of a message without concealment or alteration. The speaker is responsible for conveyance, not for forcing acceptance.
Choosing an appropriate message, method, time, and tone when inviting others to faith. Wisdom means beneficial and truthful delivery, not silence about truth.
Reasoned disagreement conducted through the most truthful, respectful, and effective means. The expression concerns both the quality of the argument and the manner of presenting it.
Promoting what revelation and sound moral judgment recognize as right. It requires knowledge, appropriate authority or ability, likely benefit, and avoidance of greater harm.
Seeking to prevent recognized wrongdoing through lawful, proportionate means. It is not a licence for vigilantism, humiliation, or uninformed interference.
Working to remove wrongdoing according to one's authority, ability, and the likely consequences. Prophetic teaching distinguishes action, speech, and inward rejection.
Understanding which duties, harms, and benefits deserve precedence. It prevents secondary matters from displacing essential obligations.
Accurate understanding of the real circumstances relevant to applying religious guidance. Knowledge of context supplements rather than replaces knowledge of revelation and law.
The foreseeable outcomes and downstream effects of actions. Ethical and legal judgment may consider consequences as well as immediate intention.
Blocking an otherwise permissible means when it is strongly expected to lead to prohibited harm. The word "means" is more accurate here than "excuses.".
Preventing or removing genuine harms and corrupting consequences. The term refers to substantive harm, not merely what someone dislikes.
Securing genuine benefits recognized by revelation and sound reason. It does not mean pursuing private advantage at any cost.
Hearts becoming mutually familiar, harmonious, and connected. It describes relational cohesion created through mercy and shared good.
Coming together upon compatible aims after difference. It can be communal concord, not only political alliance.
Arabic variations + translation: اِئْتَلَفَ (verb) — unite; be harmonious | مُؤْتَلِف (adjective) — harmonious; allied

Meaning: Submitting a dispute to an agreed adjudicator for a ruling. It can be legal, familial, or political and requires defined authority.
Arabic variations + translation: حَكَّمَ (verb) — arbitrate; appoint an arbitrator | مُحَكَّم (noun) — arbitrator; appointed judge

Meaning: Interceding to secure a legitimate benefit or prevent harm. It must not corrupt justice, cancel another person's rights, or privilege someone undeserving.
God-given human dignity that forbids humiliation and unjust violation. In other contexts, the same word can also mean an extraordinary grace granted to a righteous person.
A neighbour who is unrelated, more distant, or outside one's close circle. Qur'anic commentators differ on the exact shade of meaning, so the phrase should not be translated mechanically.
A neighbour who is also near through kinship or close proximity. It combines overlapping claims of neighbourhood and closeness.
Wrongfully severing family relationships that one is religiously required to maintain. The word for kinship is literally connected with the womb but functions as an idiom.
Obligatory financial maintenance owed to specified dependants. It is a legal duty with scope determined by relationship, means, and custom.

The husband's responsibility for maintenance, protection, and accountable leadership within the family. Interpretations differ on its scope, but it denotes duty and responsibility rather than intrinsic human superiority.
Conducting married life according to recognized goodness, fairness, and kindness. The standard is shaped by revelation and sound custom.
Repose, security, and settled companionship within marriage. It refers to emotional and relational tranquillity, not housing alone.
A solemn and weighty covenant; in family sermons, the binding marriage bond. "Weighty" expresses seriousness, not physical thickness.
The legally recognized marital union or marriage contract. In some legal and textual contexts, the word can also refer to consummation.
A binding agreement formed through offer, acceptance, and valid conditions. Its root image is tying, which explains its legal sense of contract.
The obligatory marital gift owed by the husband directly to the wife. It belongs to her and is not payment for purchasing her.
The marital gift given to the wife as a sign of serious commitment. It is closer to "dower" than "dowry" in English usage.
A marriage proposal or engagement process before the marriage contract. With different vowel marks, the same written form can mean a formal sermon.
A close relative whom a person is permanently forbidden to marry because of blood relationship, breastfeeding, or marriage. Temporary marriage prohibition does not by itself create mahram status.
A person of the opposite sex who is not a mahram and is therefore legally marriageable in principle. The category is legal and does not imply unfamiliarity or untrustworthiness.
Parts of the body or areas of vulnerability that must be covered or protected in a particular legal context. The exact scope varies by person and situation.
Protecting family privacy and dignity while responsibly addressing wrongdoing. It does not justify concealing abuse, silencing victims, or preventing access to help.
Consultative family decision-making that respects roles and affected members. It is principled consultation, not necessarily majority voting.
Serious marital breach, defiance, or failure to fulfil core marital duties. Qur'anic and juristic discussions can apply the concept to either spouse, so context is required.
Separation, abandonment, or deliberate distancing. Its ruling depends on the cause, duration, manner, and resulting harm.

A form of marital dissolution initiated by the wife, commonly involving agreed compensation. It is distinct from divorce pronounced by the husband and does not imply that freedom is being purchased as property.
Annulment or rescission of a marriage or other contract because of a legally recognized cause. It is distinct from divorce pronounced by the husband.
A prescribed waiting period after divorce or widowhood. Its length and legal purposes vary by circumstance; it is not always a mourning period.
Restoration of a revocably divorced marriage during the waiting period. It has legal conditions and is not ordinary reconciliation after any divorce.
Sponsoring, protecting, and caring for an orphan while preserving the child's biological lineage. It differs from adoption that legally replaces parentage.
Legally attributing an adopted child as one's biological child with resulting lineage effects. This is distinct from the highly encouraged care and sponsorship of orphans.
A found or abandoned child whose parentage is unknown and who is entitled to protection, identity safeguards, and care. The term does not imply moral blame or proven illegitimacy.
A traveller cut off from resources and entitled to assistance. It is a Qur'anic idiom meaning "the stranded traveller.".
A person whose available resources do not adequately meet basic needs. It is an economic and legal category, not an insult meaning miserable.
A person or group made weak through oppression, exclusion, or structural powerlessness. The passive form highlights imposed vulnerability, not inferior worth.
A person burdened by legitimate debt who may qualify to receive obligatory alms. It does not mean every borrower or every bankrupt person.
Freeing an enslaved person. The phrase uses "neck" as a metonym for the whole human being.

A historical legal category for non-Muslim subjects protected by a covenant under a Muslim polity. The term belongs to a particular juristic and historical framework and should be explained rather than equated with modern citizenship.
A non-Muslim person or party protected by a treaty or covenant. Their safety and rights arise from the binding agreement.
A person granted temporary security and protected entry. The grant of safety creates legal inviolability, not mere hospitality.
A binding grant or pledge of safety and non-aggression. In legal usage, it creates enforceable protection rather than only a feeling of security.
Coming to know and recognize one another across peoples and groups in a way that supports cooperation and rejects contemptuous hierarchy.
Arabic variations + translation: تَعَارَفَ (verb) — get to know one another; become acquainted | مُتَعَارَف عَلَيْهِ (adjective) — customary; commonly accepted

Meaning: The genuine welfare of the community as a whole. It is not automatically identical to the preference of rulers, majorities, or the state.
A recurrent social custom that Islamic law may consider when it is established, relevant, and not contrary to revelation. An occasional or corrupt habit does not qualify.
Alternative context meaning(s): Different lexical sense: crest/mane; raised ridge.

Meaning: The religious legal classification attached to an act or situation, such as obligatory, recommended, permissible, disliked, or forbidden. It is a technical ruling, not a personal opinion.
Binding adjudication of disputes by an authorized judge applying Islamic legal principles. Here "qada" means judicial judgment, not divine destiny.
A scholar qualified to derive legal rulings through disciplined interpretation of evidence. The title requires extensive competence, not personal independence of thought alone.
A coherent school of legal interpretation, principles, and accumulated juristic reasoning. It ordinarily means a school of law, not a religious sect.
Alternative context meaning(s): General intellectual context: school of thought; ideological position.

Meaning: The principles and methods governing how Islamic legal rulings are derived and how evidence is evaluated. It is not a list of elementary rules.
Derived practical rulings and subsidiary legal questions. They are applications distinguished from foundational creed and from the principles used to derive law.
Authoritative textual wording; in legal theory, it can also mean wording whose indication is especially clear. Written passages can differ in their degree of decisiveness.
The meaning most immediately indicated by wording while remaining open to reinterpretation when stronger evidence requires it. It is a technical level of textual indication, not superficial reading.
Alternative context meaning(s): Theological context: al-Ẓāhir, 'the Manifest', a divine name.

Meaning: Wording interpreted away from its more apparent sense because of valid evidence. The interpretation is evidence-based and need not always be figurative.
Wording whose intended detail is not independently clear and therefore requires explanation. It does not simply mean a concise summary.
A text or explanation that clarifies wording that was general, compressed, or uncertain. In legal theory, it means clarified rather than merely obvious.
Wording that encompasses all members of a class unless qualified. It is a technical scope category, not merely vague language.
Wording restricted to particular members or cases. It means legally specific, not confidential.
An unqualified expression referring to an instance without a limiting attribute. It is a technical semantic category, not necessarily metaphysical absoluteness.
An expression limited by a stated quality, condition, or circumstance. It is read with related evidence according to methodological rules.
Extending a known legal ruling to a new case because both share the same effective legal cause. It is structured juristic analogy, not loose resemblance.
The legally operative attribute because of which a ruling applies. It is distinct from the broader wisdom or benefit served by the ruling.
The benefit, purpose, or wise consideration served by a legal ruling. It may explain a rule without being the exact legal trigger for applying it.
The higher objectives and purposes protected and advanced by Islamic law. They are systemic goals, not an individual's private intention.
The indispensable interests whose loss gravely damages religious and human life. In maqasid theory, they commonly include religion, life, intellect, family or lineage, and property.
Needs that remove substantial hardship without reaching the level of indispensable necessity. They form a technical middle category between necessities and refinements.
Refinements that complete dignity, ethics, cleanliness, and social beauty. They are not trivial luxuries, even though they rank below necessities and major needs.
A genuine benefit recognized by revelation and sound reason. It does not mean private advantage or whatever appears useful in the short term.
A public benefit not specifically affirmed or rejected by a text but consistent with the objectives of Islamic law. Jurists use it under disciplined conditions, not to override revelation.
Preferring a stronger equitable or evidentiary consideration over an otherwise applicable analogy. It is a technical legal method, not choosing what feels pleasant.
Arabic variations + translation: اِسْتَحْسَنَ (verb) — approve; consider good | مُسْتَحْسَن (adjective) — approved; favorable

Meaning: Presuming that an established state continues until evidence proves a change. Examples include the presumption of innocence or continued ritual purity.
Arabic variations + translation: اِسْتَصْحَبَ (verb) — accompany; take along

Meaning: The presumption that no obligation or liability exists without evidence. It concerns legal burden, not a claim that a person is morally perfect.
